title: Recover an interrupted recorded update to a verified state
actor: An engineer responsible for an interrupted recording operation
goal: Complete the exact prepared update or restore its verified prior state without overwriting unrelated work or inventing new decisions.
context: A previous supported write was interrupted and the change cannot be used as a coherent current snapshot.
trigger: The engineer obtains the available transaction identity and explicitly chooses completion or restoration.
preconditions: The engineer supplies the selected change, transaction, expected recovery identity, and supported recovery action.

interaction.action: Explicitly requests completion of the prepared update or restoration of its verified prior state.
Checks available recovery information, the observed targets, and any freshness conditions required by the selected action.
Returns the verified recovered result or an explicit safe stop while preserving foreign content and the supported recovery boundary.
Reads the resulting coherent state before relying on the restored or completed work.

expected_outcome: The selected exact recovery outcome is established and attributable, without replaying semantic operations against newer content or rolling back acknowledged success.

alternatives.condition: The engineer chooses restoration of an uncommitted initial creation.
alternatives.outcome: Only transaction-created content and empty created directories are removed; preexisting or externally added content remains.

alternatives.condition: The transaction already records acknowledged commitment.
alternatives.outcome: Only supported completion/cleanup is available; saved success is not rolled back.

failures.condition: Recovery information is missing, tampered, unsupported, or a target has an unrecognized third state.
failures.outcome: The system stops without guessed repair, conversion, or overwrite of the foreign state.

failures.condition: Completion basis changed or recovery is interrupted again.
failures.outcome: The system reports the bounded stop or remaining recovery state and permits an explicit later attempt with refreshed recovery identity.
